andrewl6097 opened issue #15356:

Description

#12932 (44.0.0) stopped emitting csdb on aarch64 by default and added the aarch64 Cranelift setting use_csdb to opt back in. docs/security.md points embedders to that setting. Enabling it, though, makes Engine::check_compatible_with_native_host reject the engine, so no module can be compiled or loaded on an aarch64 host:

compilation settings are not compatible with the native host

Caused by:
    don't know how to test for target-specific flag "use_csdb" at runtime

Engine::new succeeds. The error comes from the check that Module::new and Module::deserialize* run first. Engine::precompile_module doesn't run it, so precompiling succeeds and loading the result fails. That check returns Ok for target-specific flags that need no host support, such as use_bti and sign_return_address*, and looks up the rest in the host's CPU features. use_csdb is on neither list, so it hits the final _ arm. On 43.0.x and earlier there was no flag, and csdb was emitted whenever Spectre mitigations were on.

Steps to reproduce

On any aarch64 Linux host:

let mut config = wasmtime::Config::new();
unsafe {
    config.cranelift_flag_enable("use_csdb");
}
let engine = wasmtime::Engine::new(&config)?;
wasmtime::Module::new(&engine, "(module)")?; // fails

Versions

Affects 44.0.0 through 51.0.0-rc.1, and main at 7d316a1b6. We hit it on Amazon Linux 2 and 2023 (aarch64) with 51.0.0-rc.1.

Expected

CSDB is encoded in the hint space and runs as a NOP on CPUs that don't implement it, so, like use_bti, it needs no host detection and should be accepted.

I have a fix with a test ready and will open a PR for it. Since use_csdb is the only way to get csdb back on aarch64, could it go into 51.0.0 as well?
